researchMaterialAssessment: The supplied Mars_Analogues_Haneen_Ayman.json discusses Río Tinto, Atacama, Iceland Highlands, and McMurdo Dry Valleys; it does not contain the five supplementary site records or site-specific citations. The records below are separately sourced and remain qualified by their evidence granularity.

fieldEvidenceClassificationPolicy.coordinates: Reported geographic coordinates from cited publications; DMS-to-decimal conversions are derived representations. Every point coordinate is flagged approximate because positional uncertainty is not quantified or because it identifies a study area/cluster rather than an exact outlet or sample.
fieldEvidenceClassificationPolicy.geologicalDescriptions: Published descriptive context only, retained as narrative with its citation; not promoted to a verified local lithology measurement.
fieldEvidenceClassificationPolicy.climateElevationAndGlIm: Missing/not retrieved for all supplements at review time. These are null, not zero.
fieldEvidenceClassificationPolicy.mineralClaims: Not encoded as mineral evidence. No mineral inference from general geology or lithology.
fieldEvidenceClassificationPolicy.temporalCoverage: No new time series or field measurement period is claimed in the normalized supplementary records.

sites.name: Dallol Hydrothermal Field
sites.granularity: Approximate study-area coordinate, not an individual pool/sample
sites.identityEvidence: Dallol hydrothermal field in the Danakil Depression; published study-area coordinate 14.24 N, 40.30 E.
supportedClaims: Hydrothermal field and evaporitic setting are described in the cited research.
sites.mineralEvidence: No mineral list copied into normalized mineral evidence; claims require sample-level traceability.
limitations: Coordinate is rounded and represents a study area, not a selected sampling pool.
No site-specific climate/DEM/GLiM data has been retrieved yet.

sources.citation: A geophysical multi-parametric analysis of hydrothermal activity at Dallol, Ethiopia (2010)
Origin and Evolution of the Halo-Volcanic Complex of Dallol: Proto-Volcanism in Northern Afar (2019)

sites.name: Dalangtan Playa sampling pavement, Qaidam Basin
sites.granularity: Published sampling pavement coordinate; local composite sampling field, not a playa-wide point representation
sites.identityEvidence: A primary study reports samples from a pavement at 38°35′44″N, 90°59′06″E; coordinate converted to decimal degrees without implying GPS accuracy beyond publication precision.
supportedClaims: The cited study documents collection of surface and below-rock soils at the stated pavement.
sites.mineralEvidence: No mineral claims inferred or copied into normalized minerals.
limitations: Sampling field is local and does not represent the entire playa.
The reported coordinate precision is not a quantified uncertainty estimate.
No site-specific climate/DEM/GLiM data has been retrieved yet.

sources.citation: Metabolic versatility of soil microbial communities below the rocks of the hyperarid Dalangtan Playa (2024)
The Polygonal Surface Structures in the Dalangtan Playa, Qaidam Basin (2018)

sites.name: Semail Ophiolite
sites.granularity: Large geological formation; no point selected
sites.identityEvidence: The Samail/Semail Ophiolite is a broad, mapped mafic-ultramafic geological formation extending across northern Oman and the UAE; cited work documents distinct field localities, demonstrating that one generic point would be misleading.
supportedClaims: The formation includes mafic-ultramafic units; cited work distinguishes multiple field locations and lithologic contexts.
sites.mineralEvidence: No mineral record asserted for the region as a whole.
limitations: Point-based climate, DEM, and GLiM retrieval unavailable until a named field segment is selected.
Do not use regional name as a single sample locality.

sources.citation: Tracing Carbonate Formation, Serpentinization, and Biological Materials With Micro-/Meso-Scale Infrared Imaging Spectroscopy in a Mars Analog System, Samail Ophiolite, Oman (2021)

sites.name: Gypsum Hill cold saline springs, Axel Heiberg Island
sites.granularity: Named spring system; coordinate locates the cluster, not each outlet
sites.identityEvidence: Gypsum Hill spring system, Expedition Fiord; published coordinate 79°24′30″N, 90°43′05″W. Kept distinct from Colour Peak and Lost Hammer systems.
supportedClaims: The cited field studies describe perennial cold saline springs and characterize the Gypsum Hill system.
sites.mineralEvidence: Do not generalize precipitate/mineral observations across all outlets or across Axel Heiberg Island.
limitations: Cluster coordinate is not an outlet coordinate.
No site-specific climate/DEM/GLiM data has been retrieved yet.

sources.citation: High Arctic saline springs as analogues for springs on Mars (2002)
Biological Characterization of Microenvironments in a Hypersaline Cold Spring Mars Analog (2017)

sites.name: Dasht-e Lut (Lut Desert) aeolian analog region
sites.granularity: Study region with published geographic bounds; no single sample coordinate selected
sites.identityEvidence: A published transverse aeolian ridge study defines its study region within 29°30′–30°49′N and 57°47′–59°53′E; region bounds do not identify one representative point.
supportedClaims: The cited work studies aeolian ridge landforms and their morphometry in the Lut Desert.
sites.mineralEvidence: No comprehensive mineral survey is claimed or encoded.
limitations: Point-based climate, DEM, and GLiM retrieval unavailable until a specific landform/sample is selected.
Regional study results do not describe all of Dasht-e Lut.

sources.citation: A terrestrial analog for transverse aeolian ridges: Environment, morphometry, and recent dynamics (2016)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Lut Desert
